shared_components.rationale: Nine queries join lineitem to orders on l_orderkey=o_orderkey. Building a single 15M-entry hash table on o_orderkey with payload columns (o_custkey, o_orderdate, etc.) avoids 8 redundant hash constructions. At ~200ms per build, this saves ~1600ms total across the batch. The orders dense_pk index provides row_id lookup, but a hash with pre-loaded payload columns eliminates repeated random column reads during probe-heavy joins from the lineitem side.
shared_components.notes: Consumers Q3, Q5, Q10, Q18 may drive from orders side in some plans; the hash still enables flexible plan choice. Q4 and Q13 access orders differently (scan/LEFT JOIN) and are not consumers.

shared_components.rationale: Six queries probe customer by c_custkey from an orders/lineitem join stream. Building one 1.5M-entry hash table once (~35ms) eliminates 5 redundant builds, saving ~175ms. Payload includes all commonly needed customer columns (c_nationkey for nation joins in Q5/Q7/Q8/Q10, c_mktsegment for Q3 filter, c_name/c_acctbal for Q10/Q18 output).
shared_components.notes: Q13 (LEFT OUTER JOIN) and Q22 (NOT EXISTS anti-join) iterate customer as the driver and do not probe this hash. Customer has a dense_pk but the hash pre-loads all payload columns for cache-friendly probing.

shared_components.rationale: Eight queries probe supplier by s_suppkey (Q5/Q7/Q8/Q9/Q21 from lineitem joins, Q2 from partsupp, Q15 from CTE, Q20 for IN-list check). Building the 100K-entry hash once (~8ms) saves 7 redundant builds (~56ms). Payload includes s_nationkey (needed by Q2/Q5/Q7/Q8/Q9/Q20/Q21 for nation joins) and output columns (s_name, s_address, s_phone, s_acctbal, s_comment).
shared_components.notes: Supplier has a dense_pk and supplier_nationkey_grouped index, but the hash bundles all payload columns for cache-friendly probing. Entire table (~6MB) fits in L3 cache.

rejected_candidates.reason: Full lineitem scan sharing considered for Q1, Q18 subquery, and other lineitem-heavy queries. However, most queries (Q8, Q9, Q17, Q19, Q20, Q21) access lineitem via selective indexes (lineitem_partkey_grouped, lineitem_suppkey_grouped, lineitem_orderkey_idx) rather than full scans. With 376GB RAM, OS page cache ensures column files are loaded once from HDD and reused across queries. Only Q1 (98.6% selectivity) and Q18's subquery perform true full scans, and they need different column sets (7 vs 2 columns), limiting sharing benefit.

Seven queries (Q2, Q8, Q9, Q14, Q16, Q17, Q19) join to part by p_partkey. However, Q2/Q8/Q9/Q16/Q17/Q19 all DRIVE from part with selective filters (p_type LIKE, p_brand =, p_name LIKE, p_size IN) and scan part directly, not probing it from the lineitem side. Only Q14 probes part from lineitem (780K probes, 1 month scan). With only 1 probe-side consumer, the hash build would not be shared.

Materializing the lineitem-orders join result would produce ~60M rows (every lineitem row matches exactly one order). The materialized result would consume ~3.6GB and double the I/O vs. using the hash_orders_by_orderkey component for on-the-fly probing.

Q6 and Q20 both filter lineitem by l_shipdate in [1994-01-01, 1995-01-01). However, Q20 accesses lineitem via a correlated subquery probing by (l_partkey, l_suppkey) using grouped_fk indexes, not a sequential scan. Only Q6 performs a scan (with zone map assistance). One consumer does not justify a shared component.

Q4 [1993-07-01, 1993-10-01) and Q10 [1993-10-01, 1994-01-01) have adjacent 3-month date ranges on orders. Merging to a 6-month superset would serve only 2 consumers, scanning ~1.17M rows (~15ms build cost). The 15ms savings does not justify the coordination overhead, especially with zone maps on o_orderdate available for each query independently.
Nation table has only 25 rows. Any lookup completes in <0.1ms. The accounting overhead of managing a shared component exceeds the savings.
Region table has only 5 rows. Trivially cheap to scan or hash independently. No sharing benefit.

The storage design already includes a partsupp_composite_hash index (open-addressing hash on (ps_partkey, ps_suppkey) with 16M capacity). Building a redundant in-memory hash would duplicate existing infrastructure.
